summary: This CSS file styles a ProjectSetup component that reuses visual patterns from other parts of the design system. It defines the layout for a container with a toolbar header, content area with a scrollable script section, and action buttons that start subtle but highlight in the primary color on interaction.

explanations.8: The 'composes' keyword pulls in all the styles from the 'mk-surface' global class, so this element inherits that base styling without repeating the code.
explanations.14: Similarly, this composes the 'mk-toolbar' global class to get the header's foundational styles.
explanations.18: The 'composes' keyword here brings in 'mk-eyebrow' styles for the title text — it's a way to reuse design tokens across components.
explanations.26: Setting max-height to 400px makes the script area scrollable if its content gets too tall, preventing it from dominating the page.
explanations.37: The 'var(--mk-danger-line)' is a CSS custom property (variable) that stores the danger color defined elsewhere in the design system.
explanations.41: Again using 'composes' to inherit the 'mk-toolbar__actions' styles, which likely provides spacing and alignment for a group of buttons.
explanations.48: This sets the buttons to use the monospace font family from the design system, which is typical for code or technical interfaces.
explanations.51: The buttons use a soft ink color by default, making them less prominent until you interact with them.
explanations.63: On hover, the background changes to a subtle overlay color (likely a semi-transparent layer) and the text shifts to the primary brand color.
